vulnerabilities.description: CSV injection vulnerability: The csvCell() function escapes quotes but does not handle formula injection. If audit detail fields contain values starting with =, +, @, or -, Excel/Sheets will interpret them as formulas. While audit data is server-controlled, any user-supplied note field could be exploited.

Information disclosure: Error message reveals source kind information ('This source is {kind}') which could be used for reconnaissance. Consider using generic error messages for failed kind verification.

No input validation for field value character encoding. While length is checked and hostname validated for specific fields, other public values should have more explicit character set restrictions to prevent injection vectors.
Missing rate limiting: No rate limiting on POST endpoints. Attackers could trigger resource-intensive run creation (pipeline invocation) rapidly, causing denial of service.

recommendations: Fix CSV injection in audit export: Add checks for formula prefixes (=, +, @, -) in the csvCell() function and prepend a space or quote to sanitize them
Implement rate limiting on API endpoints that trigger expensive operations (POST /api/runs, POST /api/sources, etc.) using Next.js middleware or a dedicated rate limiting library
Review information leakage in error messages - use generic messages for failed resource access/type verification while logging details server-side
Add input validation for non-hostname public fields in OAuth authorize flow to restrict to expected character sets and prevent unexpected encoding issues
Verify CSRF protection: Confirm that Next.js and Clerk middleware provide CSRF protection for state-changing operations (currently not visible in provided code)
Ensure all database credentials (DATABASE_URL, OAuth secrets, CANON_CREDENTIAL_KEY) are stored in a secrets manager rather than .env files in production
Add security headers: Implement CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options headers in middleware
Consider adding request signing to API responses to prevent tampering with exported data that leaves the system
